name_zh: 上下文无关语言的性质
canonical_name: Context-free-language closure and non-closure theorem family
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only 'closure properties of CFLs'. It does not enumerate operations, distinguish positive closure from non-closure, fix alphabet or grammar conventions, state binders or hypotheses, or select a single theorem versus a bundle. Choosing reversal, union, concatenation, star, homomorphism, regular intersection, arbitrary intersection, complement, or a conjunction at intake would invent, weaken, strengthen, or potentially falsify the received target.
domain_and_universes: Open: an admitted source must fix the terminal alphabet and universe, finiteness or decidability assumptions, words and languages, context-free grammar or equivalent automaton model, grammar finiteness and epsilon conventions, and operation-specific source and target alphabets.
conclusion: Open: no particular preservation implication, non-closure counterexample, enumerated conjunction, or classification result is selected by the repository record.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before exact source selection. Empty alphabets, empty and universal languages, the singleton empty-word language, zero-fold star, empty indexed families, epsilon productions, erasing homomorphisms, and witness grammar edge cases require explicit statement decisions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: closure of context-free languages under finite union
closure under homomorphic image and inverse homomorphism
closure under intersection with a regular language
non-closure under arbitrary intersection and complement
one conjunction or classification record containing some or all of these branches
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty terminal alphabet and languages over it
empty language, universal language, and the language containing only the empty word
epsilon productions and nullable start symbols
zero iterations in Kleene star and star versus positive closure
empty versus finite versus arbitrary union families
intersection partner regularity and its witness encoding
grammar nonterminal types and finite rule representation
excluded_substitutions: positive closure under arbitrary intersection or complement
intersection of two arbitrary context-free languages substituted for intersection with a regular language
THM-M-0761 pumping lemma, THM-M-0763 Chomsky hierarchy, or THM-M-0764 pushdown automata as the root
the pinned reversal theorem selected as the entire catalog target without an admitted source crosswalk
a custom predicate or structure that stores the desired closure conclusion as a premise
the catalog verified label, a theorem name, a finite computation, or a discovery-only probe treated as proof evidence
